solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Journalist was pen deployed more than half full-time

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread out into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: only a portion exceeding half of the word is kept, so its tail is dropped

parts.note: a full-time job is a permanent one

explanation.surface: A writer's pen was put to work for most of a full-time job.
explanation.walkthrough: PERMAN is six of PERMANENT's nine letters, comfortably more than half; NEWSPA + PERMAN gives NEWSPAPERMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaperman is someone employed in writing or editing for a newspaper, so a journalist.

clue.text: Receiving frantic SOS near chemist, one dishes out orders

indicators.note: something that receives takes other material into itself, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Boots is the big British high-street chemist chain

indicators.note: frantic means wildly agitated, so the distress call's letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
by means beside or near

explanation.surface: A pharmacy takes a panicked distress call while one person barks instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a chain of British high-street pharmacies; the scrambled distress call and 'near' go inside its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bossyboots is a domineering person who is always telling others what to do.

clue.text: Typical of dandy: 'It's a mistake imbibing water abroad'

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so one word swallows another

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder
the French word for water

explanation.surface: A traveller's warning against drinking the local water, framed as the remark of a fop.
explanation.walkthrough: Bish is informal British for a blunder; 'abroad' points to the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a dandy, and the suffix -ish forms an adjective meaning like or characteristic of one.

clue.text: Antelope brooded about it with another one coming up

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round another

parts.note: a hen that brooded sat on its eggs
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a second antelope: a gnu

explanation.surface: An antelope sat brooding, and a second one appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another one' means another antelope, since the definition is Antelope: a gnu. S(IT)AT then A GNU upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitatunga is an African antelope of swamps and marshland.

clue.text: Unknown song went out of use

parts.note: algebra uses x, y and z as unknowns
an ode is a lyric poem or song

explanation.surface: An obscure song fell into disuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went out of use' looks like the whole meaning, but it is 'went' plus a tag saying the word is obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Yode is an archaic past tense of go, so it is an obsolete form of went.

clue.text: Hooter messily blown — one runs inside (7, two words)

indicators.note: inside means placed within the other letters
something done messily is untidy and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a means one
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A horn or hooter is blown untidily while someone runs indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R go into BLOWN and the whole is mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl is jokingly called a hooter after its call, and the barn owl is a familiar species.

clue.text: Measure of grain that's capital, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved round to the end of the word

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A grain measurement that is a capital one, read from start to end.
explanation.walkthrough: ROME with its R moved to the back gives OMER.
explanation.definitionFit: The omer is a Hebrew dry measure, a tenth of an ephah, used for grain.

clue.text: Appropriate climbing haunt, round heart of Hindu Kush

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards
round means surrounding, so the resort word encloses the letter

parts.note: a resort is a place one frequently goes, a haunt

indicators.note: the heart of a phrase is its central letter

parts.note: the fifth of nine letters

explanation.surface: Seize the chance to climb a favourite mountain range in central Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: RESORT upwards is TROSER, which goes round the U from the middle of HINDUKUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser is British slang for pocketing money, so to appropriate it for oneself.

clue.text: Cornish tea's wasted — I trash this maybe

definitions.text: Cornish tea's wasted — I trash this maybe

indicators.note: wasted means ruined, so the remaining letters are wrecked into a new order
to trash something is to throw it away, so those letters are discarded

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, removed
taken as written, removed

explanation.surface: Someone ruins a Cornish cream tea and throws away a part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I, T, R, A, S, H from CORNISHTEAS to leave C, O, N, E, S, then mix them. The whole clue also describes the answer: a scone is part of a Cornish tea that might be trashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cornish cream tea is served with scones, clotted cream and jam, so a scone is what such a tea could lose.

clue.text: New students among rest breaking for a drink?

definitions.note: plural noun; the question mark admits the clue is loose

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the students go inside
something breaking falls apart, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
freshmen are first-year students

explanation.surface: First-year students take a break from the others to go for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New students' is a single chunk, not N for new plus a word for students.
explanation.definitionFit: Refreshments are food and drink, what you would offer someone wanting a drink.

clue.text: Numskull in Scotland local stir turned a lower animal

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the dialect word is read backwards

parts.note: jee is a Scots dialect verb meaning to stir or move
it is the pronoun used for an animal

explanation.surface: A Scottish fool stirs up trouble locally and turns into a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' marks a dialect word; and we call an animal 'it', not he or she.
explanation.definitionFit: Eejit is the Scots and Irish pronunciation of idiot, so a fool or dimwit.

clue.text: Packs round middle of match supported by sound boosters

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its third letter

parts.note: the central letter
amps are amplifiers, which boost sound

explanation.surface: Packing a matchstick round with something propped on loudspeakers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supported by' puts AMPS beneath the T.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamp is to pack material down firmly, as round an explosive charge in a borehole.

clue.text: Cap: gypsy's going round in one

indicators.note: in means placed within the other word

parts.note: the ace counts as one in cards

indicators.note: going round suggests turning back on itself, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Rom is a Romani man

explanation.surface: A traveller's cap is going round in one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An amorce is a percussion cap, the small explosive charge used in a toy pistol.

clue.text: Pale little fellow: one announces a special need (6, two words)

parts.note: wan means pale
tad is an American word for a small boy

explanation.surface: A pale child who has special needs.
explanation.walkthrough: Tad as a small boy is American, short for tadpole.
explanation.definitionFit: A want ad is a small classified advertisement stating what the advertiser wants.

clue.text: The misguided err with money to give fresh cover?

indicators.note: misguided means led astray, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
oof is old slang for money

explanation.surface: The foolish make mistakes when they have cash to spend on new cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The misguided' sounds like people, but 'misguided' shuffles the next word. The question mark warns that cover here means a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: To reroof a building is to put a new roof on it, a fresh covering overhead.

clue.text: Tan enveloping woman's white vesicle in the exoderm

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap round, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to sun oneself is to tan
a dame is a woman

explanation.surface: A suntan covers a woman's skin with a white blister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman's' reads as woman is, giving DAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudamen is a small whitish blister in the outer skin caused by retained sweat.

clue.text: Conductor left waistcoat in pawn

indicators.note: in places those letters within the betel word

parts.note: pawn (paan) is betel; siri is another name for betel
L is the abbreviation for left
vest is the American word for a waistcoat

explanation.surface: A conductor pawned the waistcoat he left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pawn' is not the chess piece or a pledge: pawn or paan is betel leaf, as is SIRI. Constantin Silvestri was a Romanian-born conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Constantin Silvestri led the Bournemouth Symphony Orchestra in the 1960s, so he is a famous orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Writer's trollop caught in foul den

indicators.note: in places the single letter within the den word

parts.note: a pit is a squalid hole of a place
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An author's loose woman is trapped in a filthy hovel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' flags a word used by one particular author: a painted woman, from the Picts who painted their bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary usage made a Pict of a heavily made-up woman, a painted trollop.

clue.text: Concert: I refer to one receiving word

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert
taken as written
see is the reference instruction, as in 'see page 10'

explanation.surface: Someone at a concert tells the audience to look elsewhere for news.
explanation.walkthrough: Word here means a promise, as in giving your word.
explanation.definitionFit: A promisee is the person to whom a promise is made, the receiver of someone's word.

clue.text: Nourishing drink — complaint over it being reduced with flowing water (7, two words)

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the short word loses a letter

parts.note: beef is slang for a grievance
taken as written
ea is a dialect word for a river or stream

explanation.surface: A grumble about a tonic drink being watered down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' in a down clue puts the complaint on top; ea is a dialect word for a running stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef tea is a broth made from stewed beef, traditionally given to invalids for nourishment.

clue.text: Notice youngster pinching vehicle after parking

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: to pinch is to squeeze between two fingers, so the youngster holds the vehicle

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A sign warns about a young car thief, once he has parked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinching' also means stealing, which makes the surface a car theft.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a printed sign or poster displayed in public, a notice.

clue.text: Imported horses run in principality

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the country name

parts.note: Wales is often called a principality
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Horses brought in from abroad are exercised in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Welsh ponies, but the horses are from New South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Walers were horses bred in New South Wales and exported, especially to India as cavalry mounts.

clue.text: Peeled fruit almost useless, decayed

indicators.note: peeling strips the outside, so the first and last letters go
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
useless means no use

explanation.surface: Fruit, skinned and nearly worthless, has gone rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Useless' expands to NO USE before losing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruinous can describe a building fallen into ruin, dilapidated and decayed.

clue.text: Disinfectant that's no help in fracture

indicators.note: a fracture is a break, so the letters are broken up and reset

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An antiseptic that does nothing for a broken bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fracture' plays on the medical surface, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenol, also called carbolic acid, was the first widely used antiseptic and disinfectant.

clue.text: Aide briefly admitting love for old dupe

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: asst is the abbreviation for assistant
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: An assistant, in love, is made a fool of by an old trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' marks the answer as an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Assot is an obsolete verb meaning to befool or infatuate, so to dupe.

clue.text: Vision aid? One not required by eagles, say, silly

indicators.note: silly means scatterbrained, so the letters are muddled
something not required is left out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a means one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eagles have no use for a spectacle lens, given their keen sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is part of the fodder; one A comes out of EAGLESSAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeglass is a single lens such as a monocle, worn to help a person see.

clue.text: Rent, formerly restrained, going up — one against being trapped

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means read from the bottom
something trapped is held inside, so those letters go within

parts.note: dry humour is restrained, understated
Roman numeral for one
v is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: Rent once controlled now rises, and a tenant who objects is stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' is a past participle, torn, not a payment. 'Formerly' marks Spenser's archaic form.
explanation.definitionFit: Yrivd is an archaic past participle of rive, to tear, so it means torn or rent.

clue.text: What has branches round Italy? Fundamentalist church

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the tree word encloses the letter

parts.note: an elm is a tree, which has branches
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Asks what organisation has branches throughout Italy, and answers with a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branches' suggests the church's own branches; here it is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Elim is a Pentecostal denomination, a fundamentalist evangelical church founded in Ireland in 1915.

clue.text: Cheese fly flies off in no time

indicators.note: something that flies off departs, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: done briefly is done quickly
taken as written, removed

explanation.surface: A fly leaves a piece of cheese in an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese with an edible white rind.

clue.text: Large chest in Church containing reverse of new bones

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the church abbreviation goes round

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the following letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: N is short for new
ossa is Latin for bones, used in anatomy

explanation.surface: A big chest in a church holds bones, the latest put in last.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassone is a large Italian Renaissance chest, often richly carved, used for a bride's linen.

clue.text: Dancer not dancing after removal of CD

indicators.note: once these are removed, the remaining letters are what is left

parts.note: someone calmed down is still, not dancing about
taken as written, removed

explanation.surface: A dancer stops dancing when the music disc is taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: C and D are taken from separate ends of CALMED, not as a block.
explanation.definitionFit: An alme is an Egyptian dancing girl, one who sings and dances professionally.

clue.text: Ancient deity dispersing harm, invested with indefinable quality

indicators.note: to be invested with is to be clothed in, so something is put inside
dispersing scatters things, so the letters spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
it is that special something, sex appeal

explanation.surface: An ancient god scatters harm and has a mysterious aura.
explanation.definitionFit: Mithra is the old Persian god of light and contracts, also worshipped by Romans as Mithras.

clue.text: Plenty to do? One involved no longer washing

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: having a lot on means having plenty to do
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Busy with lots of tasks, one person no longer does the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' tags the definition as an obsolete sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotion once meant the act of washing, from Latin lotio; the sense is now obsolete.

clue.text: What's coming? Hail and rain from the east avoiding area

parts.note: ave is Latin for hail, a greeting

indicators.note: in an across clue, from the east means read right to left
avoiding means leaving out, so the area letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
A is short for area

explanation.surface: Asks what weather is approaching: hail and rain blowing in from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail' looks like weather beside rain, but it is the greeting AVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Avenir is French for the future, borrowed into English for what lies ahead.

clue.text: Angler's quarry to advertise round river

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the advertising word encloses the letter

parts.note: to tout is to advertise or solicit custom
R is short for river

explanation.surface: Something an angler seeks advertised around the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout are a freshwater game fish that anglers most commonly fish for.

clue.text: Action men are dead unfortunate once beset by sclerosis

indicators.note: beset means surrounded, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: DS, disseminated sclerosis, was the older name for multiple sclerosis
taken as written
d is short for dead
evil in an old sense means unlucky or unfortunate

explanation.surface: Tough guys are dead, sadly, once struck by a wasting disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks DS as an outdated medical abbreviation; ARE, D and EVIL sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Daredevils are reckless people who do dangerous stunts, the type to be called action men.
